name: Bezaleel and Aholiab
charge: Making all that the Lord commanded, and no more; and teaching others to do it
summary: Two men were called by name and filled with the spirit of God in wisdom, understanding, knowledge and all manner of workmanship, to devise the work of the tabernacle in gold, silver, brass, stone and timber. They made every piece to the pattern shewed in the mount, and Moses looked upon all the work and blessed them. God also put in their hearts that they might teach.
offense: The obedience is exactness in craft, which the record treats as seriously as any other obedience in the volume. They worked to a pattern given on the mount and are commended for adding nothing to it: according to all that the Lord commanded Moses, so the children of Israel made all the work (Exodus 39:42). Bezaleel was of Judah and Aholiab of Dan, one of the least of the tribes, which the account sets side by side without comment (Exodus 31:2,6). The same chapter that lists their filling with the spirit lists it as being for cutting stones and carving timber (Exodus 31:5), so the first men in scripture said to be filled with the spirit of God were filled for manual work (Exodus 31:3).
judgment: Moses did look upon all the work, and behold, they had done it as the Lord had commanded (Exodus 39:43), even so had they done it: and Moses blessed them. The glory of the Lord filled the tent they had made (Exodus 40:34). They were also given the capacity to teach, so the skill was not held privately, and the tabernacle they built stood for four centuries and every case in Leviticus and Numbers takes place inside or around it.

verses.text: And the Lord spake unto Moses, saying,
See, I have called by name Bezaleel the son of Uri, the son of Hur, of the tribe of Judah:
And I have filled him with the spirit of God, in wisdom, and in understanding, and in knowledge, and in all manner of workmanship,
To devise cunning works, to work in gold, and in silver, and in brass,
And in cutting of stones, to set them, and in carving of timber, to work in all manner of workmanship.

And I, behold, I have given with him Aholiab, the son of Ahisamach, of the tribe of Dan: and in the hearts of all that are wise hearted I have put wisdom, that they may make all that I have commanded thee;
And Moses said unto the children of Israel, See, the Lord hath called by name Bezaleel the son of Uri, the son of Hur, of the tribe of Judah;
And he hath filled him with the spirit of God, in wisdom, in understanding, and in knowledge, and in all manner of workmanship;
And to devise curious works, to work in gold, and in silver, and in brass,
And in the cutting of stones, to set them, and in carving of wood, to make any manner of cunning work.
And he hath put in his heart that he may teach, both he, and Aholiab, the son of Ahisamach, of the tribe of Dan.

Them hath he filled with wisdom of heart, to work all manner of work, of the engraver, and of the cunning workman, and of the embroiderer, in blue, and in purple, in scarlet, and in fine linen, and of the weaver, even of them that do any work, and of those that devise cunning work.
According to all that the Lord commanded Moses, so the children of Israel made all the work.
And Moses did look upon all the work, and, behold, they had done it as the Lord had commanded, even so had they done it: and Moses blessed them.

text.text: And Hur begat Uri, and Uri begat Bezaleel.

entries.commentary: The Lord called by name Bezaleel the son of Uri, the son of Hur, of the tribe of Judah, and filled him with the spirit of God, in wisdom, in understanding, in knowledge, and in all manner of workmanship, to devise cunning works, to work in gold, in silver, in brass, in cutting of stones, and in carving of timber. With him the Lord gave Aholiab the son of Ahisamach, of the tribe of Dan, and put wisdom in the hearts of all that were wise hearted, that they might make all that he had commanded. The Most High still works the same way. Brothers and sisters come into the congregation who are carpenters, plumbers, electricians, builders, painters, cooks, and tech savvy, and he sets every one in the body as it pleases him; no one appoints himself over the camp or the kitchen. All the diverse gifts together build the work today the way the tabernacle was built then.

The wise hearted made all that was commanded: the tabernacle of the congregation, the ark of the testimony, the mercy seat that is thereupon, all the furniture of the tabernacle, the table and his furniture, the pure candlestick with all his furniture, the altar of incense, the altar of burnt offering with all his furniture, and the laver and his foot. They made the cloths of service, the holy garments for Aaron the priest and the garments of his sons to minister in the priest's office, the anointing oil, and the sweet incense for the holy place, according to all that the Lord commanded. That spirit of workmanship on Israel is why the tabernacle, and later the house Solomon built for the Lord, outshined anything the world had seen; and though strangers shall build up our walls in the kingdom, it will be Israel directing how the Lord wants it done.

Verily my sabbaths ye shall keep, for it is a sign between me and you throughout your generations, that ye may know that I am the LORD that doth sanctify you. Keeping the weekly sabbath and the feast days shows that Israel are his children and he is their God; the nations do not have this sabbath, and adopted Sunday worship is not the true sabbath given to the children of Israel. Every one that defileth the sabbath shall surely be put to death. The stoning was done away in Christ, but the judgment for breaking the sabbath still stands, and people still die on the sabbath day, Friday sundown to Saturday sundown; the Most High is justified, because it is his sign between him and his people. Six days may work be done, but in the seventh is the sabbath of rest, holy to the LORD. It is more than a day of rest and congregating; it is the sign of who Israel's God is, which is why saying the sabbath is done away takes away the very sign between Israel and God.

The children of Israel shall keep the sabbath, to observe the sabbath throughout their generations, for a perpetual covenant; it is a sign between the Most High and the children of Israel for ever, for in six days the LORD made heaven and earth, and on the seventh day he rested, and was refreshed. Christians use [Mark 2:27](/bible/mark/2#v27) to say the sabbath is done away, but that is not what Christ said. The sabbath was made for man, the children of Israel; man was not put on the earth for the sabbath, the sabbath was put on the earth for man, and the Son of man is Lord of the sabbath because Christ instituted it. He rested for our sakes, that we should rest after the same similitude.

When he had made an end of communing with Moses upon mount Sinai, he gave him two tables of testimony, tables of stone, written with the finger of God. God literally wrote the testimony with his finger, and we know that was Christ.

Moses gathered all the congregation of the children of Israel: six days shall work be done, but on the seventh day there shall be to you an holy day, a sabbath of rest to the Lord; whosoever doeth work therein shall be put to death. Ye shall kindle no fire throughout your habitations upon the sabbath day: kindling fire goes to cooking. Bake that which ye will bake today, and seethe that ye will seethe, and lay up what remains to be kept unto the morning; you could not cook on the sabbath, so the day before is the prep day, and what you prepare that day is what you eat.

Whosoever is of a willing heart, let him bring the Lord's offering: gold, silver, and brass; blue, purple, scarlet, fine linen, and goats' hair; rams' skins dyed red and badgers' skins; shittim wood; oil for the light and spices for the anointing oil and the sweet incense; and onyx stones and stones to be set for the ephod and the breastplate. These are the offerings the people would bring unto the Lord.

Every wise hearted among you shall come and make all that the Lord hath commanded: those who had skill, the crafty ones. The list runs through the whole work: the tabernacle, his tent, his covering, his taches, boards, bars, pillars, and sockets; the ark of the covenant with the staves and the mercy seat, and the vail of the covering; the table with his staves and vessels and the shewbread; the candlestick, which is the menorah, with his lamps and the oil for the light; the incense altar; the altar of burnt offering, where the burnt offering was burnt, with his brasen grate; the laver; the hangings of the court; and the cloths of service, the holy garments for Aaron the priest and the garments of his sons, to minister in the priest's office.

The congregation departed from the presence of Moses, and they came, every one whose heart stirred him up and every one whom his spirit made willing, and brought the Lord's offering for the work of the tabernacle; the people brought the gold and silver and all the things listed willingly. Both men and women, as many as were willing hearted, brought bracelets, and earrings, and rings, and tablets, all jewels of gold; and every man with whom was found blue, purple, scarlet, fine linen, goats' hair, red skins of rams, badgers' skins, silver, brass, or shittim wood brought it. All the women that were wise hearted did spin with their hands; the women knew how to sew, and brought that which they had spun of blue, purple, scarlet, and fine linen, and the women whose heart stirred them up in wisdom spun goats' hair. The rulers brought onyx stones, stones for the ephod and breastplate, spice, and oil.

The Lord called by name Bezaleel the son of Uri, the son of Hur, of the tribe of Judah, and filled him with the spirit of God, in wisdom, in understanding, and in knowledge, and in all manner of workmanship; the Most High put His spirit on him to be gifted in what he did, to devise curious works in gold, silver, and brass, in cutting of stones, and in carving of wood. He hath put in his heart that he may teach, both he and Aholiab the son of Ahisamach, of the tribe of Dan; the two brothers the Most High was dealing with in workmanship trained and taught their fellow brethren how to do it. It is the same today: the Most High puts His spirit on brothers and sisters with different talents, and they put their talents to use and teach others in the congregation; Israel was putting their talents together and building, showing each other how to do these works.

Chapter 39 is the application of the instructions of chapter 28: the holy garments for Aaron the priest, the clothes of service to do service in the holy place, made of the blue, purple, and scarlet as the Lord commanded Moses.

The breastplate carried four rows of stones, and the stones were according to the names of the children of Israel, twelve according to their names, like the engravings of a signet, every one with his name according to the twelve tribes; the shoulders of the ephod carried onyx stones graven the same way, stones for a memorial to the children of Israel. The Most High had us representing: when the priest stepped on the scene you already knew what nationality he was. Nationality is very important to the Lord, and he took it very seriously.

The pomegranates and the bells of gold went upon the hem of the robe round about; the word keeps saying round about, because the fringes go all throughout the garment, round about, not gathered only at four corners. Old depictions show Israelites with the fringes all the way around, and it would not hurt to put them all throughout, out of the fear of God.

They made the plate of the holy crown of pure gold, written like the engravings of a signet, HOLINESS TO THE LORD, fastened on high upon the mitre with a lace of blue. Black man, this is your heritage: our forefathers the priests wore crowns of real pure gold. It is a blessing to come back to this knowledge; they will not teach you this anywhere else.

Thus was all the work of the tabernacle finished, and the children of Israel did according to all that the Lord commanded Moses; they brought every piece to Moses, and he looked upon all the work, and behold, they had done it as the Lord had commanded, and Moses blessed them. It is like getting a building today and doing all the painting, sanding, nailing, and screwing, and then standing back and seeing the finished product: all praises to the Most High, we did it; then the people are blessed.
